📌   cURL Complete Guide (Beginner   →   Advanced)  This document consolidates   all cURL knowledge and use-cases   discussed earlier, structured for  backend development, API testing, auth debugging, CORS debugging, and production usage . 1️⃣  What is cURL?  curl   (Client URL) is a   command-line tool   to transfer data using URLs. Used for: - API testing - Backend debugging - CI/CD pipelines - Auth & CORS testing - Server health checks Basic syntax:  curl   [options]   URL 2️⃣  Basic Requests  Simple GET  curl   https://example.com  Include response headers  curl   -i   https://example.com  Headers only (HEAD request)  curl   -I   https://example.com 3️⃣  Working with APIs  GET JSON API  curl   http://localhost:3000/api/users  1Pretty-print JSON  curl   http://localhost:3000/api/users   |   jq  POST JSON  curl   -X   POST   http://localhost:3000/api/users -H   "Content-Type: application/json" -d   '{"name":"Abhishek","role":"dev"}'  PUT / PATCH  curl   -X   PUT   http://localhost:3000/api/users/1 -H   "Content-Type: application/json" -d   '{"role":"admin"}'  DELETE  curl   -X   DELETE   http://localhost:3000/api/users/1 4️⃣  Debugging & Inspection (Critical)  Verbose mode (MOST IMPORTANT)  curl   -v   http://localhost:3000/api/test  Shows: - DNS resolution - TCP connection - Request headers - Response headers  Silent mode  curl   -s   http://localhost:3000/api/test  Status code only  curl   -o   /dev/null   -s   -w   "%{http_code}
"   http://localhost:3000/api/test  2Measure response time  curl   -w   "
Time: %{time_total}s
"   -o   /dev/null   -s   http://localhost:3000/api/ test 5️⃣  Headers, Auth, Cookies  Custom headers  curl   -H   "Authorization: Bearer   TOKEN"   http://localhost:3000/api/profile  Multiple headers  curl   -H   "Authorization: Bearer   TOKEN" -H   "X-Request-Id:   123" http://localhost:3000/api/profile  Basic Auth  curl   -u   username:password   http://localhost:3000/api/admin 6️⃣  JWT Authentication Flow  Login and get token  curl   -X   POST   http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login -H   "Content-Type: application/json" -d   '{"email":"test@mail.com","password":"123456"}'  Access protected route  curl   http://localhost:3000/api/profile -H   "Authorization:   Bearer <JWT_TOKEN>"  Debug invalid / expired token  curl   -v   http://localhost:3000/api/profile -H   "Authorization:   Bearer INVALID_TOKEN"  37️⃣  Cookie-Based Auth (Sessions / NextAuth)  Save cookies after login  curl   -c   cookies.txt   -X   POST   http://localhost:3000/login -d   "email=test@mail.com&password=123456"  Use cookies in next request  curl   -b   cookies.txt   http://localhost:3000/dashboard  Inspect Set-Cookie  curl   -i   http://localhost:3000/login  Debug cookie-based auth  curl   -v   -b   cookies.txt   http://localhost:3000/dashboard 8️⃣  CORS Debugging with cURL ⚠️  cURL does NOT enforce CORS, but it can   simulate browser behavior .  Preflight (OPTIONS request)  curl   -X   OPTIONS   http://localhost:3000/api/data -H   "Origin:   http://localhost:5173" -H   "Access-Control-Request-Method:   POST" -H   "Access-Control-Request-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization"  Expected headers  Access-Control-Allow-Origin Access-Control-Allow-Methods Access-Control-Allow-Headers  Actual request with Origin  curl   -v   http://localhost:3000/api/data -H   "Origin:   http://localhost:5173"  4Cookies + CORS  curl   -v -H   "Origin:   http://localhost:5173" -b   cookies.txt http://localhost:3000/dashboard  ❌   Access-Control-Allow-Origin:   *   is INVALID with credentials. 9️⃣  Files & Forms  Upload file  curl   -X   POST   http://localhost:3000/upload -F   "file=@image.png"  Form data  curl   -X   POST   http://localhost:3000/contact -F   "name=Abhishek" -F   "message=Hello"  Download file  curl   -O   https://example.com/file.zip  Rename file:  curl   -o   myfile.zip   https://example.com/file.zip  🔟   Advanced / Backend Usage  Follow redirects  curl   -L   http://example.com  Force HTTP method  curl   -X   OPTIONS   http://localhost:3000/api/test  5Send raw body  curl   -X   POST   http://localhost:3000/raw --data-binary   "hello   world"  Timeout  curl   --max-time   5   http://localhost:3000/api/test  Rate limiting / slow client  curl   --limit-rate   10k   http://localhost:3000/api/test 1️⃣1️⃣  cURL vs Postman  cURL  Best for: - Backend debugging - CI/CD - SSH servers - Middleware testing - Learning HTTP deeply  Postman  Best for: - OAuth flows - Team collaboration - API exploration - Environment variables - Documentation  Rule of Thumb  Situation   Tool Quick API check   cURL Debug middleware   cURL CI pipeline   cURL Auth exploration   Postman Team testing   Postman  🔑   Golden cURL Habits  Always start with   curl   -v  Inspect headers before body Use   -X   only when required Use   -o /dev/null   for clean output Combine with   jq  1.  2.  3.  4.  5.  6🏁   Final Cheat Sheet  curl   -v   URL curl   -X   OPTIONS   URL   -H   Origin:... curl   -H   "Authorization: Bearer   ..." curl   -c   cookies.txt curl   -b   cookies.txt curl   -o   /dev/null   -w   "%{http_code}"  📌   Final Note  If you can debug   auth ,   CORS , and   middleware   using only cURL —   👉   you understand HTTP at a  backend-engineer level .  7
